# Contributing

Thanks for your interest in contributing to this LSD Open Terraform module. This
is the canonical contributing guide shared across all LSD Open Terraform modules;
it is synced into each module repo from
[`lsdopen/.github`](https://github.com/lsdopen/.github/blob/main/.github/terraform/CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Code of Conduct

This project follows the [CNCF Code of Conduct](https://github.com/cncf/foundation/blob/master/code-of-conduct.md).
By participating, you are expected to uphold it. Please report unacceptable
behaviour to the module maintainers.

## Reporting issues

Use the repository's issue tracker. Before opening an issue:

1. **Search existing issues** to avoid duplicates.
2. **Provide reproduction steps** for bugs, with the Terraform and AWS provider
   versions in use.
3. **Describe the use case** clearly for feature requests.

## Pull requests

We follow the standard fork-and-pull workflow:

1. **Fork** the repo on GitHub.
2. **Clone** your fork to your machine.
3. **Create a branch** for your change.
4. **Commit** using [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
   subjects (`feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`, `chore`, `ci`, …).
5. **Push** to your fork.
6. Open a **Pull Request** describing what changed and why.

## Code standards

- **Formatting**: all code must pass `terraform fmt -recursive`.
- **Linting**: all code must pass `tflint` (shared config is fetched from
  `lsdopen/.github` when no local `.tflint.hcl` exists).
- **Security**: all code must pass the Trivy config scan with no HIGH/CRITICAL
  findings (shared config from `lsdopen/.github`; override with a local
  `trivy.yaml`).
- **Naming**: `kebab-case` for files and folders, `snake_case` for resources,
  variables, outputs and locals.
- **Documentation**: every variable and output must have a `description`. The
  README inputs/outputs tables are generated by `terraform-docs` — do not edit
  them by hand.

## Local validation

Before opening a PR, run:

```bash
terraform fmt -recursive
terraform init -backend=false && terraform validate
tflint --init && tflint
trivy config .
```

## Release process

Modules use semantic-release: version bumps and tags are created automatically
from Conventional Commit history when changes merge to `main`.
